transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thanks for seeing me, I really appreciate it. 

Um... I guess what made me finally ask for help is... well, I barely want to eat anymore. It's probably not a huge deal, but, like, I'll be on my lunch break at the store, and I'll just sit there staring at food I used to really like. And I just end up throwing most of it away. I don't mean to be wasteful or anything, I just can't bring myself to eat it. 

Is that... does that make sense to come in for? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, even activities you once liked?

Um, yeah, I guess I have noticed that a little bit. I hope it's okay to admit this, but... well, I used to get really excited about things. Like going to gallery nights, or playing basketball, or even just grabbing food-truck tacos. I also used to help kids out with art stuff, which I know is a really good thing to do, and I don't want you to think I'm a bad guy or lazy for not wanting to do it right now... but lately, when I try to do any of that, I just stand there feeling kind of... flat? 

Like, I just can't get into it anymore, no matter how hard I try to put on a good face. I usually end up making up some excuse to leave early so I don't bring anyone else down. 

Is that... I mean, is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you been feeling like you’re a burden to others or that you’re not good enough lately?

Um, well... I guess I've been feeling a little bit like that, yeah. I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or anything, because I know I have a lot to be grateful for. 

But, um... at work, they recently gave me this employee award, and they even talked about me maybe trying for a supervisor spot. Which is really nice of them, and I made sure to thank them, but... I just keep thinking I don't really deserve it. I feel kind of guilty, actually, like I somehow tricked everyone into thinking I'm better at my job than I am. 

People keep telling me I earned it and that I didn't trick anyone, but I just can't shake this feeling that I'm not good enough for it. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm ungrateful or anything... does that make sense? Is that what you meant?
Have you noticed that you feel more tired than usual, even after getting enough rest?

Um, yeah... I have noticed that a little. I mean, I know working retail is supposed to be tiring, and I really don't want to sound like I'm whining about my job, because I'm lucky to have it. 

But... lately, by the middle of a shift, my body just feels really heavy. Like, even doing the simple stuff I normally don't mind, like straightening the clothing racks or walking back to the stockroom... it just takes so much more out of me than it should. I try to push through it so my manager doesn't think I'm slacking off, but it's just really hard right now. 

Is that normal? I mean, I hope I'm not making a big deal out of nothing... is that the kind of tired you meant?
Have you noticed that your thoughts have been moving more slowly than usual, or that your body feels physically slowed down, like you're moving through molasses?

Um, I don't think so? I mean, I try really hard to stay on top of things, especially at work. I don't want anyone thinking I'm holding up the line or, you know, not pulling my weight. 

I guess I haven't really noticed feeling like I'm moving through molasses or anything like that. My thoughts feel pretty normal to me, I think. But maybe I'm just not paying close enough attention? I hope that's an okay answer. If you need me to think about it more, I definitely can.
Have you noticed that you feel unusually restless or that you can’t sit still lately?

Um, no, I don't think I've been feeling restless or anything. I actually try to make sure I'm pretty calm, especially around other people. I wouldn't want to make anyone else nervous or uncomfortable by fidgeting all the time, you know? 

I can sit still just fine, I think. I mean, I hope I haven't been moving around too much while we've been talking? I'm really trying to be a good patient and just focus on your questions. So, yeah, no real restlessness that I've noticed. Is that... is that a good thing?
Have you been feeling like you’re not worthy of good things happening to you, or that you don’t deserve the kindness or recognition from others?

Um... well, it's a little hard to talk about, honestly. I mean, I don't want to sound ungrateful, because my manager actually gave me this Employee of the Month award recently, and they even mentioned I might have a chance to be a supervisor. Which is... it's really nice of them. 

But... I just keep thinking I don't really deserve it. Like, I feel this weird guilt, almost like I somehow tricked everyone into thinking I'm doing a better job than I actually am. My coworkers keep telling me I earned it and that I shouldn't think that way, and I try to smile and say thank you so I don't seem rude or unappreciative. But inside... I just feel like I'm a fake. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds silly. I really should just be happy about it, right? I hope it's okay that I feel this way... I'm trying to work on it, I promise.
Have you lost interest in most activities, even things you used to really enjoy doing?

Um, I mean... I guess I've been a little less active lately? I hope that's not a bad thing. I used to really love doing stuff, you know? Like going to gallery nights, or playing basketball with the guys, or even just grabbing food-truck tacos. I also used to help out with some art stuff for the kids in the neighborhood, which was always really fun.

But recently... I don't know. I try to go and be part of it so I don't let anyone down, but when I'm there, I just kind of stand around feeling... flat, I guess? Like the excitement just isn't there anymore. I usually end up making some excuse to leave early so I don't ruin the vibe for everyone else. 

I really hope I'm not sounding lazy or anything. I still want to be a good friend and do those things, it's just... harder right now. Is that normal to feel that way sometimes?
Have you felt a significant loss of energy or felt fatigued, even when you haven’t been doing much?

Um... yeah, I guess I have been a little tired lately. I mean, I don't want to complain, because my job isn't even that hard, really. I just work in retail. But... I don't know, by the middle of a shift, my body just starts to feel so heavy. 

Like, even doing simple stuff, like straightening the clothing racks or just walking back to the stockroom... it just takes so much more out of me than it should. I try really hard to push through it because I don't want my manager to think I'm slacking off, especially after they gave me that award. I always make sure I'm still smiling for the customers. 

But I definitely feel... drained, I guess? Even on my days off when I'm just sitting around. I hope I don't just sound like I'm out of shape or not trying hard enough. Is it okay that I feel that way?
How long have you been feeling this way? Have these feelings lasted for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Um... well, it's been a little while now, I think. I really hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than it is. But... yeah, I guess it's been going on for most of the day, pretty much every day, for about two months now. 

It kind of started around the time I got that award for the window display... and when the district manager started paying more attention to me. I know I should be thrilled about all of that, and I really am grateful, I promise! It's just... that's kind of when this heavy, tired feeling started sticking around all the time. 

I've been trying my best to snap out of it so I don't let anyone down. I hope it's not frustrating that it's been going on for that long... I really am trying to get better. Is two months a long time to feel like this?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating much less or much more than usual, or losing or gaining a significant amount of weight without trying?

Um... yeah, I guess there's been a little bit of a change. I really hope it's not a big deal, and I know I should be taking better care of myself, but... honestly, this is kind of what made me finally ask for help. 

I just... I barely want to eat anymore. I don't want to sound ungrateful for having food or anything, but like, I'll be on my lunch break at the store, and I'll have something I usually really like. But I just sit there staring at it. I try to take a few bites so I don't waste it, but I usually just end up throwing most of it away. 

I really am trying to eat, I promise. I don't want to get sick or make anyone worry. Is it normal to just lose your appetite like that when you're feeling tired?
Have you noticed any weight loss recently, even if you haven't been trying to lose weight?

Um... well, since I haven't been eating much like I mentioned... yeah, I guess I have lost a little bit of weight. I haven't been trying to or anything, I swear! I know I'm supposed to be keeping my strength up for work. 

I don't have a scale at home, so I don't know exactly how much, but... my work pants are definitely a lot looser on me than they were a couple of months ago. I actually had to punch a new hole in my belt just so they wouldn't look baggy. I really hope my manager doesn't think I look unprofessional or anything. 

I know I should be doing a better job of forcing myself to eat so I don't lose too much weight... I'm sorry, I really am trying. Is it okay that I lost weight just because I haven't had much of an appetite?
Have you been feeling guilty or blamed yourself for things that weren’t your fault, or felt that you were a failure or had let others down in some way?

Um... well... I guess I have been feeling a little bad about some things. I really hope it doesn't make me sound ungrateful, because I know I should just be happy about the award and the district manager noticing me. But... honestly? 

I just keep thinking that I don't deserve any of it. Like I don't deserve the award for the display, or even the chance to maybe be a supervisor one day. It's silly, I know, because people keep telling me I did a good job, but... I just feel this awful guilt, like I somehow tricked everyone into thinking I'm better at my job than I actually am. 

I really try not to let it show, because I don't want to seem like I'm complaining when good things happen. I know I should just accept it and do my best. Is it normal to feel like a fraud when people give you a compliment? I really hope I'm not overthinking everything...
Have you had episodes like this before, where you felt down, lost interest in things, and had trouble eating or sleeping, or is this the first time you've felt this way?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I really don't think I've ever felt quite like this before. I hope that's an okay answer, I know sometimes people have a history of these things, but... honestly, this is all pretty new to me. 

I've had days where I was tired or maybe a little stressed from work, but nothing like this where I just can't seem to shake it or where I'm not eating. I really try to be a positive person usually, I promise. I always try to come to work with a smile and do my best. 

So, yeah, this is the first time it's gotten... well, this noticeable, I guess. I'm sorry if that's not very helpful, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is it okay that this is the first time it's happened?
Have you had any thoughts about death, dying, or not wanting to live anymore?

Oh... um, no. No, definitely not. I really hope I didn't say anything to make you think I was... you know, wanting to hurt myself or anything like that. I promise I haven't had any thoughts about dying. 

I know I've been struggling a bit and feeling bad, but I really do want to be here and just... get back to normal, you know? I would never want to do something like that and let my team down at the store, or cause trouble for anyone. I'm trying really hard to keep pushing through it all, I swear. 

Is it okay that I don't have those kinds of thoughts? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers and not making things more complicated for you.

I just keep thinking that I don't deserve any of it. Like I don't deserve the award for the display, or even the chance to maybe be a supervisor one day. It's silly, I know, because people keep telling me I did a good job, but... I just feel this awful guilt, like I somehow tricked everyone into thinking I'm better at my job than I actually am. 

I really try not to let it show, because I don't want to seem like I'm complaining when good things happen. I know I should just accept it and do my best. Is it normal to feel like a fraud when people give you a compliment? I really hope I'm not overthinking everything...

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has had recurrent episodes of depression, which would point toward a diagnosis of recurrent major depressive disorder (F33.x) rather than a single episode (F32.x).
doctor.question: Have you had episodes like this before, where you felt down, lost interest in things, and had trouble eating or sleeping, or is this the first time you've felt this way?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about past psychiatric history (whether the patient has had episodes like this before). This is not covered in the provided symptom profiles, which only detail the current episode's symptoms, duration, functional impairment, etc.

patient.answer:
Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I really don't think I've ever felt quite like this before. I hope that's an okay answer, I know sometimes people have a history of these things, but... honestly, this is all pretty new to me. 

I've had days where I was tired or maybe a little stressed from work, but nothing like this where I just can't seem to shake it or where I'm not eating. I really try to be a positive person usually, I promise. I always try to come to work with a smile and do my best. 

So, yeah, this is the first time it's gotten... well, this noticeable, I guess. I'm sorry if that's not very helpful, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is it okay that this is the first time it's happened?

inference.note: The patient has not reported any prior episodes, ruling out recurrent depression (F33.x). This is their first episode, which narrows the list to F32.x codes. The severity can still be differentiated based on additional symptoms, so F32.1 (mild), F32.2 (moderate), and F32.3 (severe) remain under consideration.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has had thoughts of death or dying, which would support a diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder, as this is a critical symptom not yet assessed.
doctor.question: Have you had any thoughts about death, dying, or not wanting to live anymore?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about suicidal ideation or thoughts of death, which is not included in the provided Symptom Profiles.

patient.answer:
Oh... um, no. No, definitely not. I really hope I didn't say anything to make you think I was... you know, wanting to hurt myself or anything like that. I promise I haven't had any thoughts about dying. 

I know I've been struggling a bit and feeling bad, but I really do want to be here and just... get back to normal, you know? I would never want to do something like that and let my team down at the store, or cause trouble for anyone. I'm trying really hard to keep pushing through it all, I swear. 

Is it okay that I don't have those kinds of thoughts? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers and not making things more complicated for you.
